summary: feat(core): add a sandbox file journal — a host that wants to know what a sandboxed turn wrote has had to scan the tree before and after the turn and diff the two listings, which misses renames, cannot tell a write from a re-write, costs a full walk per watched root per turn (the cost #577 documents on the consumer side: 50 001 entries, ~0.8 s of per-turn I/O, and a no-op past the cap) and gives the host no vocabulary for "this listing is incomplete"; a runner can now report the writes made inside its boundary as events through a cursor-based, replayable stream, opt-in per runner and free when not requested (no goroutine, no fd, no watch registration); the contract (core/sandbox/journal.go, beside contract.go) adds FileJournal, WriteEvent (create / write / rename / remove, a Seq cursor, Session when the backend can attribute it), JournalGap (overflow / retention / capacity / watch_lost / backend — read as "unknown", never as "nothing written"), JournalOptions (exclude, ops, retention, max_watch_set), the instance-level Capabilities.Journal declaration and OpenJournal, which fails with NotAvailable when no journal is attached, with the three decorators (AllowCommands, WithApproval, WithDefaults) forwarding the journal the way they already forward Close so Capabilities never lies; the engine under core/sandbox/journal is a bounded ring (drop-oldest with an explicit retention gap, never blocking the source goroutine) that folds per-syscall noise into net state changes — a file created and written in one go is one create, a move is one rename — with directory exclusion, an ops filter where a filtered class is not a gap, and a watch budget whose overflow is a reported capacity gap rather than a quietly smaller watch set, while misconfiguration fails at build time as Validation; the sources keep the same semantics on every platform — inotify on Linux (one watch per directory, MOVED_FROM / MOVED_TO cookies), kqueue on macOS (one descriptor per watched entry, directory diffing through the directory records' own type and inode, the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE raised toward the budget) and ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows (one pending overlapped read per directory on a completion port, RENAMED_OLD / NEW_NAME pairing, ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR as an overflow) — with no new dependencies (x/sys only) and no cgo, FSEvents rejected for exactly that reason; local, bwrap, seatbelt and windows all attach a journal, via WithFileJournal or the deployment's journal: settings, and a platform without a source fails the host build instead of producing a runner that reports nothing, while bwrap watches writable_paths entries at their host absolute paths because a namespace backend sees the same files, not the same paths; core/sandbox/internal/journaltest holds one contract suite (create, write, rename, remove, folding, exclusion, budget, retention, gap, unattributed Session) that runs against every backend in each platform's own commands (/bin/sh on the unices, cmd /c on Windows) — bwrap through a real namespace on the integration_bwrap tag, seatbelt through sandbox-exec, windows through cmd, and local wherever it has sessions to drive at all; docs/guides/sandbox.md gains the settings and the semantics (observation, not enforcement; bounded; unattributed on the Linux source) together with the config skill's references, CI gains a darwin lane that runs core/sandbox/... (kqueue source, contract suite, seatbelt through sandbox-exec) and the bwrap lane now makes bubblewrap usable on Ubuntu 24.04, where AppArmor's unprivileged-userns restriction otherwise fails it with "setting up uid map: Permission denied" before it can run the integration tests the lane exists for; the push Watch wrapper over the same ring and a privileged WriterID source stay documented future work; chore(core,driver/openai): migrate to the OTel attribute log API — go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log v0.19.0 carries GO-2026-6615 (the batch processor busy-spins once its export buffer is full) and otlptrace v1.43.0 carries GO-2026-6505, the first fixed log SDK release is v0.21.0, and the family only moves as one because sdk/log and otlploghttp both require otel/log at the matching version and that release is the attribute-based rewrite — log.Value, log.KeyValue, the log.Kind* constants and the log.String/Int/Int64/Bool constructors are gone, record bodies and attributes are attribute.Value / attribute.KeyValue — so every core telemetry producer swaps to the attribute vocabulary (attribute.String/Int/Int64/Bool, attribute.KeyValue, attribute.Value), Value.Kind() becomes Value.Type() and the Kind* constants become attribute.STRING/BOOL/INT64/FLOAT64, FormatPlainTextRecordLine drops its "String() returns a type name for non-string kinds" special case because attribute.Value.String() renders every scalar kind and the KindBytes branch goes away with the type it switched on (attribute has no bytes kind), the tests let logtest.RecordFactory disable the attribute limits itself rather than supplying the removed AttributeCountLimit / AttributeValueLengthLimit fields and compare string(kv.Key) because kv.Key is an attribute.Key, and driver/openai takes the same swap for its single telemetry attribute; core/go.mod moves the otel family to v1.45.0 / v0.21.0 (sdk/log, log, logtest, otlploghttp) with otlptrace, otlptracehttp and otlpmetrichttp at v1.45.0 and the tidy fallout (logr 1.4.4, grpc-gateway 2.29.0, genproto 2026-08-03, proto/otlp v1.11.0), which clears both advisories inside core and unblocks downstream consumers, who cannot lift sdk/log past them on their own while the vulnerable module is compiled from this repository; the driver/openai tag, cut by hand on main, must be tidied against this core before it is cut — its go.mod still requires core v0.4.4 and otel/log v0.19.0, and driver code built against an older core cannot compile against the attribute-based telemetry helpers.
